Counsel for Respondent :- G.A.,Ashwani Kumar Singh,Ashwani Kumar Singh(Amicus Curaie)
Hon'ble Saurabh Lavania,J. 
1.

On being mentioned by the counsel for the appellant for taking up the appeal out of turn in view of
the fact that the marriage of the sister of the appellant would be solemnized today, i.e., on
16.04.2024 and reception party would be held on 19.04.2024, the appeal is taken up out of turn.

2. Heard Mr. Sadab Siddique, advocate, holding brief of Mr. Saud Rais, counsel for the appellant,
Mr. Rao Narendra Singh, learned A.G.A. for the State and Mr. Ashwani Kumar Singh, Amicus Curiae appointed by the Court vide order dated 08.02.2024.
3.

The present appeal has been filed under Section 14-A (2) of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes Act, 1989 against the impugned order dated 08.01.2024, passed by Special Judge, SC/ST Act,
Lucknow, in Bail Application No.10482 of 2023, arising out of F.I.R/ Case Crime No. 128/2023,
under Sections 493, 376, 504, 506 I.P.C., and Section 3(2)(v) of SC/ST Act, Police Station- Cantt.,
District- Lucknow.

sentences.text: While pressing the present appeal, counsel appearing on behalf of the the appellant submitted that it is a case of consent and on account of annoyance and discord in the relationship between appellant and victim for some reason, the F.I.R. is issue was lodged by the informant/complainant (victim), wherein she levelled certain allegations against the appellant, according to which the appellant performed some rituals of marriage and thereafter made physical relationship with the victim and thereafter, as would appear from the F.I.R., the appellant refused to marry the victim.
Thus, in a nutshell, the story set up by the prosecution in the F.I.R. is to the effect that physical relationship with victim was made by the appellant by making false promise of marriage.

It is further submitted that the case of the appellant is squarely covered by the judgment(s) of Hon'ble Apex Court rendered in the case of Deepak Gulati vs. State of Haryana (2013) 7 SCC 675; Sonu @
Subhash Kumar vs. State of U.P. and Another (2021) 7 SCC; and Mandar Deepak Pawar vs. State of Maharashtra and Another 2022 SCC OnLine SC 2110.
5.

entities.text: Deepak Gulati vs. State of Haryana (2013) 7 SCC 675
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text:
Sonu @
Subhash Kumar vs. State of U.P. and Another (2021) 7 SCC;
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Mandar Deepak Pawar vs. State of Maharashtra and Another 2022 SCC OnLine SC 2110
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He also stated that as per the observations made by Hon'ble Apex Court in the above referred judgments to attract the offence under Section 376 IPC, the allegation should be to the effect that promise to marry given was false at the inception and from the F.I.R., it reflects that the said contents in its true spirit are missing.

6. He also stated that if the story in FIR is taken in its face value even then it can be deduced from the facts that complainant/ informant was aware that there existed obstacles in marriage as the appellant belong to other religion, even then the victim continued with relationship, as such, it is a case of consent.

7. He lastly submitted that all the aforesaid aspects of the case were not considered by the trial court,
as such, the present appeal is liable to be allowed and the impugned order may be set aside and the appellant be enlarged on bail.

8. Learned A.G.A. for the State as well as learned Amicus Curie appearing on behalf of the victim opposed the prayer for bail, however, he could not dispute the aforesaid contention of counsel for the appellant 9.
Considered the submissions advanced by the counsel for the appellant, learned A.G.A. for the State and all the relevant documents placed on record.

10. Upon due consideration of the facts and circumstances of the case, submissions of counsel for the appellant and learned A.G.A., F.I.R., impugned order, as also the observations made by Hon'ble Apex Court in the judgments, referred above, and the period of relationship, as also other aspects of the case, this Court is of the view that all the factual aspects of the case were not considered by the trial court in the light of the observations made in the judgments, referred above, while passing the impugned order.
For these reasons, this Court finds that the present appeal is liable to be allowed.
Accordingly, it is allowed.

11. Order dated 08.01.2024, passed by Special Judge, SC/ST Act, Lucknow, in Bail Application No.10482 of 2023, arising out of F.I.R/ Case Crime No. 128/2023, under Sections 493, 376, 504,

2 506 I.P.C., and Section 3(2)(v) of SC/ST Act, Police Station- Cantt., District- Lucknow, is hereby set aside.
12.

entities.text: Shahid vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Let appellant- Shahid be released on bail in the aforesaid case crime number on his furnishing personal bond of Rs.25,000/- (Rupees Twenty Five Thousand Only) and two reliable sureties each of the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following additional conditions :-
( i) The appellant shall cooperate with the prosecution during trial.
(ii) The appellant shall not tamper with the evidence during trial.
(iii) The appellant shall not pressurize/intimidate the prosecution witness(s).
(iv) The appellant shall not commit an offence.

(v) The appellant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.

(vi) The appellant shall remain present before the trial court on each date fixed,
either personally or through counsel.
(vii) The appellant shall not seek any adjournment on the dates fixed for evidence when the witnesses are present in court.
(viii) The appellant shall remain present, in person, before the trial court on the dates fixed for recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C.
13.
In case of default of above conditions, it shall be open for the trial court to treat it as abuse of liberty of bail and pass orders in accordance with law 14.

As this order relates to enlargement of the appellant on bail, it is clarified that observation(s)
made in this order shall have no bearing on the merits of the case and the trial court shall not be influenced by any observation(s) made in this order.
15.

Further, direction is issued to the Senior Registrar of this Court for payment of Rs.15,500/-
(Rupees Fifteen Thousand and Five Hundred Rupees Only) to Mr. Ashwani Kumar Singh, Amicus Curiae, on his moving an application before him within two weeks from the date of receipt of the aforesaid application.
